newsitem.title: USA: Indiana county considers $67 mln bonds for roads.
newsitem.headline: Indiana county considers $67 mln bonds for roads.

text.p: Hamilton County Council members are set to vote Wednesday on $67 million of bonds backed by the county option income tax for a road construction program, the county attorney said.

If approved, it will be the first time that the county just north of Indianapolis has issued debt for road projects, although it has issued lease revenue debt for the construction of a government center and jail in the past, Michael Howard said.
The six basic road projects will be financed by four to six negotiated issuances, the first $10 million of which could be sold in September or October, Howard said.
The rest of the bonds would be issued as needed into 1999, Howard said. Each issuance will require separate approval from the council.
City Securities Corp has been selected as lead underwriter for all the financings. H.J. Umbaugh & Associates is the financial adviser and Ice, Miller, Donadio & Ryan as bond counsel, Howard said.
